entry.title: Why AI Agents and Users Should Share the Same UI, Not Just MCP

media:group.media:title: Why AI Agents and Users Should Share the Same UI, Not Just MCP
media:group.media:description: Granola's Chris Pedregal on why the agent and the user should be working in the same UI at the same time, not just having the agent operate the app through MCP behind the scenes.⁣ ⁣ His take: give the agent an MCP or CLI, give the user a web interface, and sync the state between them so either one can pick up the work. That's the actual architecture for building AI products people collaborate with instead of just delegate to. #shorts

entry.title: Stop Rebuilding Internal Tools: Why You Should Trust the Stack (PostHog, Notion, Slack + MCP)

media:group.media:title: Stop Rebuilding Internal Tools: Why You Should Trust the Stack (PostHog, Notion, Slack + MCP)
media:group.media:description: Stop rebuilding your own CRM. Stop rebuilding your own dashboards. It sucks and it's not your job.⁣ ⁣ The move is trusting best-in-class tools like PostHog, Notion, Slack, and Flora, then connecting them through MCP so your models can find the context and actually do the work. The jump from 5.5 to 5.6 made that context-finding (and keeping it through long tasks) way better.⁣ ⁣ Specialization wins. Let the SaaS operators be great at their thing, let the model be great at using it.

entry.title: We Tested Claude Opus 5. It’s Frustrating with Flashes of Brilliance.

media:group.media:title: We Tested Claude Opus 5. It’s Frustrating with Flashes of Brilliance.
media:group.media:description:
We tested Claude Opus 5 for a week across coding and knowledge work. Dan Shipper breaks down where it struggled, why complex skills can make it stop early, and the counterintuitive setting that improved his results.
The early verdict: Opus 5 is hard to love. It can be pushy, break workflows built for Opus 4.8, and quit before the work is finished. Lower thinking effort and simpler prompts helped, but Dan still prefers GPT-5.6 for daily work and Fable for the biggest assignments.

entry.title: How to Build a Multi-Agent Review Swarm

media:group.media:title: How to Build a Multi-Agent Review Swarm
media:group.media:description:
Ryan Nystrom, a software engineer on Notion AI, shows Every CEO Dan Shipper how he turns a spoken brief into a sourced Notion task, working code, and a passing pull request.
Ryan talks through a real model-picker migration, lets Notion AI explore the codebase and write the plan, then hands that plan to an agent. Before anyone reviews the code, a custom multi-agent review swarm checks the frontend and backend for accuracy and sustainability. The agent opens the pull request, watches the tests, and fixes failures while Ryan is in meetings. Ryan’s key to success: Defining the goal, constraints, tools, and verification system before the agent starts on the work.
